item.title: Will Smith’s ‘Fresh Prince’ mansion gets 25% price cut to $22.95M, may face demolition
item.description: The iconic Fresh Prince of Bel-Air mansion is back on the market with a significant price reduction. This nearly century-old estate, familiar from the popular 1990s show, is now listed for $22.95 million. The property requires extensive renovation and is likely to be torn down by its new owner. The mansion, owned by Farhad Rahban for decades, boasts Colonial Revival architecture and spacious grounds.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Saudi Arabia released 313 gazelles and 20 years later both species thrived
item.description: A groundbreaking initiative saw the reintroduction of captive-bred sand and Arabian gazelles to Saudi Arabia's Uruq Bani Ma'arid protected area. Over two decades, camera traps documented the flourishing populations of these species. Sand gazelles exhibited seasonal movement patterns in the expansive desert, while Arabian gazelles adjusted their daily activities amid the extreme heat, showcasing an impressive long-term adaptability to their environment.

item.title: NYC agrees to $60M settlement with owners of 64 seized properties; Zohran Mamdani plans TPT revival
item.description: New York City has agreed to pay $60 million to owners of 64 properties seized under its Third Party Transfer program over unpaid taxes and other debts. The settlement follows a class-action lawsuit alleging owners were denied proper compensation. Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s administration is now considering reviving the controversial program with reforms.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Built in 1976, Diane Keaton bought $6.6M Laguna home, transformed, sold for $7.9M, now listed for $10.3M
item.description: Diane Keaton’s Laguna Beach home, built in 1976, was purchased by the actress for $6.6 million in 2021 and transformed before being sold for $7.9 million a year later. Now, the four-bedroom oceanfront property is back on the market for $10.3 million, with Keaton’s distinctive design touches and lighting still intact.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Meet Brooke Sumpter, 11, who learned to sew at 4 and designed an American Girl collection
item.description: Brooke Sumpter, an 11-year-old fashion designer, has made history by becoming the first child to design an American Girl fashion collection. She began learning to sew at just four and has now created the Cherry Blossom Couture Collection with Harlem’s Fashion Row and Mattel, featuring stylish outfits for American Girl’s 18-inch dolls.

Alleged Attack On Korean Streamer: Police detail premeditated charges; case remains under investigation
item.description: A South Korean streamer in her 20s was allegedly attacked by her former chat moderator at a restaurant in Ansan. Police said he held her by the neck with a weapon and poured hot water on her. More than 30 officers responded before he was arrested. Investigators are reviewing additional charges, including attempted murder and retaliatory crime.

item.title: New Texas Lakefront Home: Simone Biles moves into custom mansion; five-year build tested patience
item.description: Simone Biles and Jonathan Owens’ Texas lakefront mansion is finally complete after years of planning, approvals and construction delays. The couple started designing the home in 2020 and finished it in November 2025. The reported $3 million property includes a private gym, pool, sports court, large kitchen, spa-style bathroom, laundry room and a dedicated space for their dogs.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Pewdiepie Son Dress Debate: Old vlog clip splits viewers; he plans to end vlogs
item.description: PewDiePie has faced mixed reactions after footage of his three-year-old son, Björn, wearing dresses resurfaced from a July 2026 family vlog. While some viewers defended the YouTuber and praised his relaxed parenting, others criticised the decision and sparked debate online. PewDiePie also revealed plans to end regular vlogs involving Björn, saying he wants his son to grow up away from the internet and decide for himself if he wants to appear later.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Florida volunteer pilots started flying animals out of overcrowded shelters in 2010
item.description: A nonprofit based in Winter Park is making a significant impact by transporting over twelve thousand rescued animals to their forever homes. Volunteer pilots graciously contribute their time and aircraft for these crucial missions, linking overcrowded shelters in the South with dedicated rescue groups in the North. Additionally, Animals Away assists in emergency situations like natural disasters and hurricane evacuations, continually broadening its volunteer pilot network.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2018, Massachusetts removed the first of two old dams from former cranberry bogs; by 2020...
item.description: In a groundbreaking ecological revival, old dams on the Coonamessett River in Massachusetts were dismantled, restoring wetlands and providing passage for migratory fish. This project repurposed industrial farmland into a flourishing coastal ecosystem, allowing fish to ascend to upstream spawning spots that had been blocked for years. The restoration involved creating a sinuous stream channel and replacing a narrow culvert, establishing a model for agricultural bog transformations throughout New England.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Meet Samuel Henderson, the 12-year-old who can mimic more than 100 bird calls and is now...
item.description: Samuel Henderson, a gifted young boy, has skyrocketed to social media fame with his extraordinary ability to mimic over one hundred bird species solely using his voice. His captivating talent has enchanted audiences worldwide, accumulating millions of views. Remarkably, wild birds often respond to his lifelike calls. Samuel now passionately advocates for wildlife conservation and encourages everyone to explore the great outdoors.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Airbnb is committing $250 million to help stalled US housing projects get built
item.description: Airbnb has announced a robust initiative to inject $250 million into stalled housing projects, targeting funding shortfalls in construction-ready developments. The first investment of $6.4 million is earmarked for creating affordable housing in Austin, Texas. Additionally, a $5 million innovation prize will encourage advancements in housing technology, all part of Airbnb's commitment to tackling the persistent housing crisis in the United States.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
